verdict.root_cause: Every cartservice Redis call takes a near-constant 300-310ms for both HGET and HMSET, while cartservice handler self-time stays under ~1.3ms and no span or log line carries an error [tr_1f9ddd7bccaa, tr_ba698652f8b1]. Latency scales arithmetically with call count: GetCart ~300ms, AddItem ~600ms, frontend roots ~910-926ms. All other dependencies in the same traces are sub-millisecond to low-milliseconds [tr_1f9ddd7bccaa]. The tight floor rather than a long tail is the signature of a fixed per-round-trip injected delay, matching the traffic-shaping sidecar that the change log shows applied and reverted four times on cartservice in the preceding day [tr_bba397c639cb]. The log claims the last detach was ~1.6h before onset, but the observed behaviour says fixed delay is still in effect on the cartservice-to-redis-cart hop, so either that revert did not clear the shaping rule or a re-application went unrecorded. checkoutservice and frontend alerted because they waited on cartservice, not because they failed [tr_9e59e291b12d, tr_34f7d9e1f14e].
verdict.reasoning: Traces isolate the slow hop to cartservice-to-Redis and show the handler blocked, not busy; reads and writes, all three cart operations, and both callers are equally affected, which rules out caller-side or operation-specific causes [tr_1f9ddd7bccaa]. The symptom is waiting, not failing: cartservice logs a clean start, a passing Redis self-test, and continuous successful request handling [tr_ba698652f8b1], and callers show no error surge [tr_9e59e291b12d, tr_34f7d9e1f14e]. That excludes bad_deploy and resource_exhaustion, which would surface restarts or refusals. It also excludes bad_config in the strict sense: the REDIS_ADDR port override was reverted and startup shows the default endpoint in use, so no wrong value is breaking requests [tr_bba397c639cb, tr_ba698652f8b1]. What is left is added delay in the call path, and the only mechanism the evidence names for that is the recurring egress-shaping sidecar.
open_questions: Is the traffic-shaping sidecar or its tc rule still present on cartservice pods at 10:15, given the change log records a detach ~1.6h before onset? Direct pod/interface inspection was never dispatched.
redis-cart itself was never examined - server-side slowlog, CPU, or persistence stalls could produce a similar flat ~300ms floor.

No pre-incident latency baseline exists: returned traces cluster in 10:15:28-10:15:59 only [tr_1f9ddd7bccaa], and cartservice's error-ratio series is empty in both windows [tr_a2e03da51503], so onset timing is unconfirmed.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself became slow (server-side stall or contention), and cartservice is merely waiting on a genuinely degraded cache.
alternatives.why_not: The latency is a near-constant 300.7-309.2ms floor across reads and writes [tr_1f9ddd7bccaa], which fits a fixed injected delay far better than server-side load; no Redis-side telemetry was collected either way.

alternatives.root_cause: The REDIS_ADDR override to a non-default port was still effective at onset, sending cart traffic through a slower path.
alternatives.why_not: cartservice's startup log shows it connected to the default redis-cart:6379 and passed its self-test [tr_ba698652f8b1], and the override is recorded as reverted ~1.3h before onset [tr_bba397c639cb].

proposal.expected_effect: No change is applied, so the observable prediction is continuity: cartservice's HGET/HMSET child spans in Tempo should keep sitting in the tight 300-310ms band, GetCart ~300ms, AddItem ~600ms, frontend roots ~910-926ms, with zero error-status spans, until someone inspects the cartservice pod's egress qdisc/sidecar list and redis-cart's own slowlog and CPU. The reason for abstaining is that revert_config's second precondition is not met: the change log states positively that the traffic-shaping attach, the image bump and the REDIS_ADDR override were each reverted, the last of them ~1.3h before onset, and that no change of any kind falls inside the incident window [tr_bba397c639cb]. revert_config restores the *previous recorded* configuration for cartservice; on this change history the previous state is the fault-injection state (REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6380 plus the shaping attach), so firing it would plausibly re-apply the very delay we are trying to remove. The verdict's own mechanism - a tc rule or sidecar surviving its recorded detach - is not something this action's config restore reaches, because the surviving artifact is pod-level network state, not cartservice's env block. rollback_image fails the same window test (image reverted ~1.9h before onset) and restart_service is the closest legal candidate but its precondition, evidence pointing at process state rather than a change, is contradicted by the verdict, which names a change-derived shaping rule; a restart that recreated the container without the stale qdisc would also destroy the only remaining evidence of whether it was there.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if direct inspection of a cartservice pod shows a tc netem rule or a shaping sidecar container still attached to eth0 with a ~150ms per-direction delay, or if the change log turns out to under-record a fifth un-reverted attach - in that case the mechanism is confirmed live and detaching it (an action outside this allowlist, requiring pod-level exec rather than config restore) becomes the correct fix and every minute of abstention is customer-visible latency. It is also wrong if redis-cart's slowlog or CPU shows a server-side stall producing the same flat floor, in which case the target is redis-cart, which is not in the blast radius given to me and cannot be acted on here at all. Note that the confirming observations for either branch cannot be made from the evidence board as it stands: cartservice's calls_total series is empty in both windows [tr_a2e03da51503] and every returned trace is bunched into 10:15:28-10:15:59 [tr_1f9ddd7bccaa], so there is no latency baseline against which to measure any recovery, and onset time itself is unconfirmed. An action taken now would not be verifiable as having worked.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is elapsed time: cartservice keeps adding ~300ms per Redis round trip, frontend page loads stay near 900ms, and checkoutservice keeps blocking on GetCart/EmptyCart, so user-visible slowness continues for as long as inspection takes. That is a real cost and it grows. The risk being avoided is larger and less reversible: revert_config on cartservice would recreate the container with the prior recorded env, which this change history says was the injected-fault state, so a misfire converts a 300ms delay into a 300ms delay plus a Redis address pointing at port 6380 - a hard connection failure on a service currently reporting no errors at all [tr_ba698652f8b1], turning a latency incident into an outage.
proposal.blast_radius: Nothing changes, so no one sees anything new. For contrast, had revert_config fired: cartservice alone recreates, but its inbound edges are frontend (AddItem, GetCart) and checkoutservice (GetCart, EmptyCart via PlaceOrder) [tr_1f9ddd7bccaa], both of which would see connection resets during the recreate and lose in-flight carts; loadgenerator would register the resulting failures. Because the reverted value includes a Redis dependency address, redis-cart would also see its traffic move to a different port. All four already-alerted seeds would be affected.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerting simultaneously along the cart/checkout/frontend path is a coordinated failure, not a single stray warning. No open incident covers it, and the shared dependency behind checkout and frontend is unidentified.
